chapter_theme: A single four-line invocation (காப்பு) that is also the most quoted verse under Agasthiyar's name: if the mind is set right, there is no need to recite mantra, raise the breath or stop the vaasi, for a right mind is itself the right mantra. It places the whole of the following ஞானம் under the primacy of mind over technique.
structure_note: One அறுசீர் விருத்தம் of four lines, each beginning மனமது செம்மையானால் (if the mind is set right), the first three negating a practice (mantra recitation, raising the vital air, halting the vaasi) and the fourth affirming that the mind is the mantra. It is printed as the காப்பு of the work's second run, and 'ஞானம் - 2' is not otherwise headed.

2414.reading: If the mind is set right there is no need to recite mantra, no need to raise the vital air, no need to halt the vaasi; if the mind is set right, the mantra is itself set right.
2414.nuance: செம்மை is straightness or rightness, not mere calm. The three practices named are the Siddhars' own: japa, raising the breath along the spine, and holding the vaasi (breath as the practice). The verse does not reject them as false, it makes them unnecessary once the mind is right; the fourth line can also be read as 'the mind is the mantra', the usual way it is quoted. Whether this is a dismissal of technique or a statement of its goal is left open.

links.note: Tirumular lays down the breath measures (sixteen in by the left, sixty-four held, thirty-two out) and says this is the truth; Agasthiyar says that if the mind is set right there is no need to raise the vital air or halt the vaasi. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar means the breath practice is dispensable; if he means a right mind already does what the practice aims at, the verses need not clash.

The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and everything else is noisy show; Agasthiyar says a right mind is the whole of mantra and the breath practices are unnecessary. The same move, mind made the sole essential and outward means set aside, in ethics and in yoga.

Tirumular says silence is speech and mind both stilled, and that a silent mouth alone is mere muteness; Agasthiyar says the mantra is right when the mind is right, not when it is recited. Both place the practice's worth in the mind's state and not in the act.

new_concepts.gloss: the breath as the Siddhars' practice: the vital air raised, held and reversed along the central channel (also the 'horse' of their cipher), and the Siva-yoga built on it
new_concepts.label_source: 2414 names it: வாசியை நிறுத்த வேண்டா, no need to halt the vaasi, beside வாயுவை உயர்த்த (raising the air).

source_issues: The work's second run consists of this one verse headed காப்பு (invocation); there is no run headed ஞானம் - 2, so the numbering of the headed runs skips from ஞானம் - 1 (2405 to 2413) to ஞானம் - 3 (2420 to 2425).
